sources.evidence: The download describes the indicative extent and position of registered freehold properties in England and Wales
sources.guard: INSPIRE polygons are indicative freehold extents, not a complete title inventory, address-to-UPRN table or broadband serviceability source.

sources.evidence: The dataset is a subset of the Index Polygons database for freehold land and property
sources.guard: An INSPIRE ID is not a UPRN and the polygon subset does not cover every registered title or leasehold unit.

sources.evidence: The service provides geographic extent data for specific registered titles
sources.guard: A paid title extent still requires a separate, verified title-to-UPRN relationship and does not establish broadband availability.

sources.evidence: The collection describes authoritative address data for England, Scotland and Wales
sources.guard: Address lifecycle data and UPRNs do not supply title boundaries or current broadband orderability.
Relationship packages do not themselves provide full title polygons or prove that a relation remains valid after source-feature changes.

sources.evidence: The API is an OpenData service for property, street and OS MasterMap identifier relationships
sources.guard: An API relationship response supplies identifiers and metadata, not a legal boundary or broadband serviceability result.

sources.evidence: OS Open TOID lists OS MasterMap identifiers with a generalised location
sources.guard: A generalised TOID location is not the source MasterMap geometry, a title boundary or proof of address/serviceability equivalence.

sources.evidence: ONS states ONSUD and NSUL are geography lookup products rather than address products
sources.guard: A UPRN-postcode association cannot prove an address is current, uniquely located within a building or broadband-serviceable.

sources.evidence: Source products can have different update cycles
sources.guard: A high relationship confidence does not provide geometry and does not establish title ownership or broadband availability.

sources.evidence: The product links UPRNs, USRNs, TOIDs and metadata
sources.guard: A BLPU-to-TopographicArea relation is a topographic/address relation, not a registered-title or guaranteed parcel relation.

sources.evidence: The product contains the position and UPRN of each included AddressBase Premium record
sources.guard: Point-in-polygon is only a candidate spatial relation and can be ambiguous for shared buildings, campuses and multi-unit premises.

sources.evidence: NSUL allocates current GB addresses to Output Areas using UPRN and point-in-polygon methodology
sources.guard: Statistical-geography allocation cannot establish a legal parcel boundary, active address status or broadband availability.

sources.evidence: The report is a January 2026 snapshot of fixed and mobile network availability
sources.guard: Aggregate coverage and checker updates do not prove installation or retail orderability at a selected parcel.

sources.evidence: Connected Nations is currently published twice a year
sources.guard: Publication cadence and aggregate performance data cannot establish current property-level speed or serviceability.

sources.evidence: The dataset links HMLR title numbers to AddressBase UPRNs where an address relationship can be made
sources.guard: The direct relationship is licensed and incomplete, and a linked title/UPRN still does not establish broadband serviceability.
